tree.name: Vinyl Recommender System Architecture
tree.description: A sophisticated **hybrid desktop application** designed to bridge the gap between digital streaming and physical vinyl collecting. The system is split into a **Python-based analytical backend**—leveraging AI, audio DSP, and web automation—and a **Vue.js-powered reactive frontend**. Communication is facilitated via a high-performance bridge provided by `pywebview`, allowing for a seamless integration of local system resources and web technologies.

children.name: Backend Analytics & Orchestration
children.description: The 'brain' of the system, responsible for audio signal processing, AI-driven taste mapping, and web-scale marketplace automation.

children.name: Application Lifecycle
children.description: Nodes managing the initialization and bridge connectivity between domains.

files.description: Serves as the **primary entry point** for the entire application, initializing the environment and loading variables. It handles the window creation via `pywebview` and ensures the integration between the Python logic and the Vite-driven frontend.

The **central orchestration layer** that exposes Python methods to the JavaScript context. It manages multi-threaded execution for background audio analysis and coordinates complex workflows between the database, clients, and AI advisors.

children.name: Intelligence Engines
children.description: Sophisticated logic modules that quantify musical taste and find physical inventory.

files.description: Interfaces with OpenAI to provide **qualitative semantic analysis** of audio data. It translates raw mathematical similarity scores into human-readable insights that explain why a specific album fits a user's unique 'Sonic DNA'.

Contains the **mathematical core of the system**, utilizing K-Means clustering and Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). It calculates the user's taste centroid and generates visual 'Sonic Maps' to plot album compatibility in a 2D PCA space.

A **Playwright-driven automation module** that navigates Dutch vinyl marketplaces to locate stock and pricing. It uses stealth techniques to avoid detection and passes raw HTML content to the LLM for high-accuracy product link extraction.

children.name: Audio Analysis Core
children.description: Tools specialized in extracting spectral features and semantic tags from raw audio signals.

files.description: Leverages the **CLAP (Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining) model** to perform zero-shot audio classification. It maps 48kHz audio signals to a large set of natural language prompts to determine the 'vibe' and 'mood' of a track.

A **semantic configuration file** that defines the hierarchical layers of prompts used by the CLAP model. It categorizes audio into Sound Sources, Energy, Mood, and Genre, providing the linguistic foundation for audio tagging.

Handles API communication with Deezer and performs **low-level spectral analysis** using Librosa. It extracts MFCCs, chroma features, and tempo from 30-second previews to feed the system's similarity engine.

children.name: Persistence & Observability
children.description: Services ensuring data integrity and system transparency across async tasks.

files.description: The **persistence layer** utilizing SQLite to store user preferences, cached CLAP results, and scanned album metadata. It enables the system to operate efficiently by avoiding redundant audio downloads and model inferences.

A **highly customized logging utility** that uses the Rich library to provide color-coded, level-specific feedback for async operations. It suppresses noisy external library logs while highlighting critical path events like AI reasoning and web scraping.

children.name: Frontend User Interface
children.description: The interactive dashboard allowing users to visualize their Sonic DNA and audit albums for potential purchase.

children.name: Interface & Reactivity
children.description: The primary views and logic governing the user's visual experience.

files.description: The **monolithic root component** that manages the application's reactive state, including sync status and analysis results. It implements complex polling logic to update the UI as the Python background workers finish multi-stage audio processing.
Standard entry point for the Vue 3 application. It **mounts the virtual DOM** and initializes global styling, ensuring the frontend is ready for the Python bridge to inject the JS API.
The HTML template that provides the **mounting point for the application**. It serves as the bridge for the Vite development server and the final production asset container.

children.name: Design & Pre-processing
children.description: Styling configurations that drive the modern dark-themed aesthetic of the app.

files.description: The **entry point for CSS injection**, importing Tailwind's base, component, and utility layers. It ensures that the application has a consistent, professional-grade visual foundation.
Configuration file for the **utility-first CSS framework**. It defines content paths to ensure unused styles are purged, keeping the production build of the desktop app lightweight.

Manages CSS transformations, specifically **handling autoprefixing and Tailwind processing**. This ensures that the frontend styling remains compatible with the specific Chromium version bundled with pywebview.

children.name: Frontend Infrastructure
children.description: The build and dependency management systems for the web layer.

files.description: Defines the **frontend ecosystem**, including scripts for development and building. It manages dependencies like Vue 3 and Vite, which are critical for the rapid prototyping of the interactive dashboard.

The **build tool configuration** that optimizes the frontend assets. It specifically sets the development server port to 5173 to allow the Python backend to reliably connect to the frontend during development.

children.name: Project Infrastructure
children.description: Deployment scripts, environmental metadata, and dependency specifications.

children.name: Development Workflows
children.description: Batch scripts used to automate environment setup and versioning.

files.description: A **comprehensive automation script** for Windows environments. It handles virtual environment creation, PyTorch hardware detection (CUDA vs CPU), and provides one-click commands for running, building, and freezing requirements.

Automates the **Git tagging and release process**. It validates the current branch status, checks for uncommitted changes, and ensures that version increments in `version.txt` are properly reflected in the repository history.

children.name: Environment & Metadata
children.description: Static files defining the technical requirements and current state of the project.

files.description: Specifies the **entire Python dependency tree**, including heavy-duty libraries like PyTorch and Librosa. It is used by the `go.bat` script to ensure that every developer has an identical analytical environment.
A simple **SemVer-compliant metadata file**. It acts as the source of truth for the `release.bat` script when generating new build artifacts and deployment tags.

children.name: Documentation & Concept
children.description: Strategic definitions and developer-centric guidelines for the project.

children.name: Technical Documentation
children.description: High-level overview and quirk-logging for project maintainers.

files.description: The **foundational philosophy document**. It outlines the 'Vinyl Uncertainty Tax' and explains the core principles of the 'No-Skip' standard that the application's logic is built to enforce.
Provides **onboarding instructions** and technical prerequisites for new contributors. It serves as the primary map for setting up FFmpeg and other OS-level dependencies required for audio analysis.

A specialized **AI-context document** designed for support programmers. It logs workarounds and atypical architectural choices to help Large Language Models better understand the project's unique codebase.
A **comprehensive project snapshot** containing the initial roadmap and tech stack definitions. It preserves the early design goals and workflow logic used to scaffold the application.
